title: "desctable Stata help file"
---

```{=html}
<div class="stata-help">
<pre>
<span class="result"><u>Title</u></span>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>desctab</u></span><span class="result">le</span> --
               Tables of Descriptive Statistics - with Unique Treatment of
               Continuous, Binary, and Nominal Variables
<br/>
<br/>
<span class="result"><u>General syntax</u></span>
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>desctab</u></span><span class="result">le</span> <i>varlist</i> [<i>if</i>] [<i>in</i>] <span class="result">,</span> <span class="result">filename(</span><i> </i><span class="result">)</span> [options]
<br/>
<a name="overview"></a><br/>
<span class="result"><u>Overview</u></span>
<br/>
    <span class="result">desctable</span> produces a descriptive (summary) statistics table. <span class="result">desctable</span>
    treats continuous, binary, and nominal variables differently -- providing
    statistics and labeled output most appropriate for the measurement level
    of the variable.
<br/>
    Factor syntax is required: binary and nominal variables must be entered
    into the variable list with the i. prefix. Variables without any prefix
    are assumed to be continuous.
<br/>
    <span class="result">desctable</span> outputs the descriptive statistics table to Excel; it can easily
    be copied to Word without losing the formatting of the table.
<br/>
    <span class="result">desctable</span> labels the rows of the table with the corresponding variable
    label.  Categories of nominal variables are labeled with the value labels
    of the corresponding variable. Thus, the effectiveness of the default
    table depends on the effectivness of the labels in the data (see label for
    details on adding variable and value labels to your data).
<br/>
<br/>
<span class="result"><u>Options</u></span>
<br/>
<a name="required"></a><br/>
        +-----------------+
    ----+ Required Option +---------------------------------------------------
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>file</u></span><span class="result">name(</span><i>string</i><span class="result">)</span>
                  is required. This names the Excel sheet that is saved with the
                  descriptive statistics table. If the filename includes spaces,
                  it must be enclosed in quotations; e.g. filename("file name
                  has spaces")
<br/>
<a name="stats"></a><br/>
        +---------------------------------------------+
    ----+ Optional statistics to include in the table +-----------------------
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>stat</u></span><span class="result">s(</span><i>string</i><span class="result">)</span>
                  specifies which statistics should be included in the table.
                  Each statistic is reported in a separate column of the table.
                  The default is <span class="result">stat(mean sd)</span> which reports the mean
                  [proportion for binary and nominal variables] and the standard
                  deviation of continuous variables.  Statistics can be
                  requested in any order desired; columns of the table will be
                  ordered based on the list specified in <span class="result">stats( )</span>. The following
                  statistics are available:
<br/>
         Stat Name    Description
         -----------------------------------------------------------
         <span class="result"><u>mean</u></span>         Mean of continuous variables; proportion of
                     binary/nominal variables.
         <span class="result"><u>sd</u></span>           Standard deviation (c).
         <span class="result"><u>freq</u></span>         Freqency for each category of a nominal
                     variable.
         <span class="result"><u>n</u></span>            Number of non-missing observations for a
                     variable.
         <span class="result"><u>var</u></span><span class="result">iance</span>     Variance (c).
         <span class="result"><u>med</u></span><span class="result">ian</span>       Median (c).
         <span class="result"><u>min</u></span>          Minimum (c).
         <span class="result"><u>max</u></span>          Maximum (c).
         <span class="result"><u>range</u></span>        Range [max - min] (c).
         <span class="result"><u>iqr</u></span>          Interquartile range [75th percentile - 25th
                     percentile] (c).
         <span class="result"><u>cv</u></span>           Coefficient of variation [sd/mean] (c).
         <span class="result"><u>semean</u></span>       Standard error of mean (c).
         <span class="result"><u>skew</u></span><span class="result">ness</span>     Skewness (c).
         <span class="result"><u>kur</u></span><span class="result">tosis</span>     Kurtosis (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p1</u></span>           1st percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p5</u></span>           5th percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p10</u></span>          10th percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p25</u></span>          25th percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p50</u></span>          50th percentile [same as <span class="result">median</span>] (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p75</u></span>          75th percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p90</u></span>          90th percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p95</u></span>          95th percentile (c).
         <span class="result"><u>p99</u></span>          99th percentile (c).
                      
         <span class="result"><u>svymean</u></span>      *Survey weighted estimate of mean; proportion
                     of binary/nominal variables.
         <span class="result"><u>svysemean</u></span>    *Survey weighted estimate of standard error of
                     mean (c).
         <span class="result"><u>mimean</u></span>       *Multiple imputation estimate of mean;
                     proportion of binary/nominal variables.
         <span class="result"><u>misemean</u></span>     *Multiple imputation estimate of standard
                     error of mean (c).
         <span class="result"><u>misvymean</u></span>    *Survey weighted multiple imputation estimate
                     of mean; proportion of binary/nominal
                     variables.
         <span class="result"><u>misvysemean</u></span>  *Survey weighted multiple imputation estimate
                     of standard error of mean (c).
<br/>
         -----------------------------------------------------------
<br/>
(c) indicates this statistic is only reported for continuous variables.
<br/>
* <span class="result">svy</span> statistics are only available if data has been svyset. 
<span class="result">mi</span> statistics are only available if data has been mi set. 
<span class="result">misvy</span> statistics are only available if data has been mi svyset.
<br/>
<a name="stats"></a><br/>
        +---------------+
    ----+ Other options +-----------------------------------------------------
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>dec</u></span><span class="result">imals(</span><i>#</i><span class="result">)</span>   changes the number of decimal places reported for the
                  statistics. The default is 2. Any integer between 0 - 5 is
                  allowed.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result">listwise</span>      performs listwise deletion across all specified variables.
                  That is, observations with missing data on any of the
                  variables included in the table are excluded from any of the
                  reported statistics.  The default is casewise deletion which
                  includes observations that are non-missing for each specific
                  statistic.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>note</u></span><span class="result">s(</span><i>string</i><span class="result">)</span>
                  adds footnotes to the bottom of the table.  The notes are
                  automatically wrapped so they do not exceed the width of the
                  table. For long lists of notes, you will need to adjust the
                  height of the cell in Excel after the table is made for all of
                  the notes to be visible. Notes must be enclosed in quotation
                  marks, e.g. notes("This is a footnote").  For long lists of
                  notes you can list the notes on multiple lines in the code, as
                  long as each line is enclosed in quotations, e.g. notes("This
                  is the first footnote" "This is the second footnote").  The
                  appearance of the notes will be unaffected.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result">title(</span><i>string</i><span class="result">)</span>
                  adds a title to the table. The default is to title the table
                  "Table #: Descriptive Statistics (N = ##)" where the N size is
                  calculated automatically based on the total number of
                  observations that descriptive statistics were calculated for.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result">font(</span><i>string</i><span class="result">)</span>  changes the font of all numbers, labels, notes, and titles in
                  the table. The default is "Times New Roman"
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>fonts</u></span><span class="result">ize(</span><i>#</i><span class="result">)</span>   changes the font size of all numbers, labels, and titles in
                  the table. The default is 11.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result">notesize(</span><i>#</i><span class="result">)</span>   changes the font size of the footnotes on the table. The
                  default is 9.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result">txtindent(</span><i>#</i><span class="result">)</span>  changes how far the statistics are indented from the right
                  edge of the column. All statistics are right-justified so that
                  the statistics align on the decimal point. The default is 1.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>sing</u></span><span class="result">leborder</span>  changes to a single horizontal line as the border on the top
                  and bottom of the table. The default is to use double
                  horizontal lines as the table top and bottom borders.
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>sheet</u></span><span class="result">name(</span><i>string</i><span class="result">)</span>
                  adds a name to the individual Excel sheet where the table is
                  saved. The default is to name the sheet "Descriptives Table"
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result"><u>varname</u></span><span class="result">s</span>      labels the rows of the table with the variable names rather
                  than the variable labels. The default is to use the variable's
                  label if it exists.
<br/>
<a name="stats"></a><br/>
        +---------------+
    ----+ Group options +-----------------------------------------------------
<br/>
<br/>
    <span class="result">group(</span><i>groupvar</i><span class="result">)</span>
                  specifies that descriptive statistics should be calculated
                  separately for each group of the nominal grouping variable.
                  Statistics for each group are added to the right of the
                  tables. Labels for the new columns are automatically generated
                  from the value labels of the grouping variable.
<br/>
<br/>
<span class="result"><u>Examples</u></span>
<br/>
    sysuse nlsw88
<br/>
    desctable wage age i.race i.union i.collgrad tenure i.occupation hours,
        filename("descriptivesEX1")
<br/>
    desctable wage age i.race i.union i.collgrad tenure i.occupation hours,
        filename("descriptivesEX2") stats(mean freq sd min max iqr median)
<br/>
    desctable wage age i.race i.union i.collgrad tenure i.occupation hours,
        filename("descriptivesEX3") font("Helvetica") fontsize(13)
<br/>
    desctable wage age i.race i.union i.collgrad tenure i.occupation hours,
        filename("descriptivesEX4") decimals(3)
<br/>
    desctable wage age i.union i.collgrad tenure i.occupation hours,
        filename("descriptivesEX5") group(race)
<br/>
    desctable wage age i.race i.union i.collgrad tenure i.occupation hours,
        ///
        filename("descriptivesEX6") ///
        notes("This is the first footnote." ///
            "This is how to split long footnotes" ///
            "onto multiple lines of the code.")
<br/>
                        
<span class="result"><u>Comments</u></span>
<br/>
    <span class="result">desctable</span> makes the descriptive statistics table using Stata's <span class="result">putexcel</span>
    command. Because of some of the putexcel features used, Stata version 14.1
    or newer is required to use <span class="result">desctable</span>.
<br/>
    Available statistics for continuous variables are those that can be
    calculated with tabstat (with the exception of <span class="result">q</span> - which is not allowed
    with <span class="result">desctable</span>). See tabstat for more details.
<br/>
<br/>
<span class="result"><u>Authorship</u></span>
<br/>
    <span class="result">desctable</span> is written by Trenton D Mize (Department of Sociology, Purdue
    University) and Bianca Manago (Department of Sociology, Vanderbilt
    University).  Questions can be sent to tmize@purdue.edu
<br/>
</pre>
</div>
```
